facts.statement: Shamosuchus lived in the Djadochta Formation of Mongolia during the Late Cretaceous, roughly 75 to 71 million years ago.
facts.quote: Shamosuchus is an extinct genus of neosuchian crocodyliform that lived during the Late Cretaceous (Campanian) period in what is now the Djadochta Formation of Mongolia, approximately 75 million to 71 million years ago.

facts.statement: Shamosuchus grew up to 4 meters long and possessed a rostrum of moderate length.
facts.quote: Shamosuchus reached up to 4 m long and had a rostrum of moderate length.

facts.statement: In S. djadochtaensis, the alveolar margin at the premaxilla-maxilla articulation is continuous and lacks a notch for the opposing mandibular tooth.
facts.quote: Where the premaxilla and maxilla articulate, the alveolar margin is continuous and is characterised by the absence of a notch for receiving the opposing mandibular tooth.

facts.statement: Shamosuchus had eyes and nostrils not positioned above the skull, requiring it to lift its entire head out of the water to breathe.
facts.quote: The eye and nasal openings were not raised above the skull as in modern crocodilians, so that the animal would have to raise its head completely out of the water to breathe.

facts.statement: Its cranial morphology suggests Shamosuchus was not an ambush predator but likely fed on aquatic invertebrates.
facts.quote: As this cranial morphology does not suit an ambush predator, it lends support to the idea of a diet of aquatic invertebrates.

facts.statement: The genus Shamosuchus was named by Charles C. Mook in 1924.
facts.quote: The genus was named in 1924 by Charles C. Mook.

facts.statement: Recent cladistic analysis suggests that the genus Paralligator is distinct from Shamosuchus, despite previous synonymization.
facts.quote: However, recent cladistic analysis of Paralligatoridae found the former genus to be distinct from the latter.

facts.statement: Shamosuchus lived in the Gobi Desert of Mongolia during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 85 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Shamosuchus es un género extinto de crocodilomorfo neosuquio que vivió durante el período Cretácico Superior (Santoniense-Maastrichtiense) en lo que ahora es el desierto de Gobi de Mongolia, hace aproximadamente 85 a 66 millones de años.

facts.statement: The time range for Shamosuchus spans from the Cenomanian to the Maastrichtian, between 100.5 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Maastrichtian (100.5 to 66 million years ago)
